messages:
brightbeam-sre: Heads up — since 2026-02-18T03:10Z our eu2 dedicated pool p95 token latency jumped from ~180ms to ~1.2s and a small fraction of requests started getting 429s. This started immediately after an autoscale event (scale down then up). Any chance this is a MIG re-packing or noisy neighbor?

anya: Sorry — that sounds bad. Can you paste a couple example request IDs + the pool id? Also confirm whether you're on a reserved dedicated pool or a shared-dedicated pool.

brightbeam-sre: request ids: r_8a3f, r_8a45. pool: eu2-dedicated-23. model: gpt-open-7b-8k-quant. We're on a shared-dedicated (not reserved) pool. Response headers include: `x-rw-error: token-throttle` and sometimes `x-rw-eviction: in-progress`.

opsbot: [alert] pool=eu2-dedicated-23 p95_latency=1200ms alert_ts=2026-02-18T03:12:05Z mig_evictions=3 last_5m sm_util_peak=95% node=gnode-47

micah: Can you run `redwoodctl node describe gnode-47 --metrics 5m` and paste NVML + KV cache stats? Also `redwoodctl pool describe eu2-dedicated-23 --last 10m` for packing events.

brightbeam-sre: pasted outputs below:
```
# nvml snapshot
node=gnode-47 sm_util=94 95 93 96 90
mig_partitions=[sliceA:1/1, sliceB:2/2, sliceC:1/1]
mig_evictions=3
kvcache_hits=22% -> 21% -> spike to 22% (then cold) -> back up
batch_size_avg=64 -> spike 512 at 03:09:42
api_errors=[429, CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT]
```

samir: That pattern matches a neighbor burst (large batch job) that forced aggressive packing changes. When slices move we see KV cache cold starts and eviction churn -> token-level throttles and 429s. The `batch_size` spike is a smoking gun.

brightbeam-sre: Confirming KV cache miss rate spiked to 78% during the window. Also captured this error snippet from client logs: `Inference failed: CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT, retrying -> returned 429 after retries`

anya: Quick mitigation options: 1) Temporarily route your traffic to a pinned isolation slice (we can create a routing rule) 2) Bump your account's autoscale min capacity to avoid scale-downs during heavy traffic windows 3) Request emergency move off gnode-47 while we investigate. Which would you like first?

micah: For triage, we should also reproduce locally: run a steady small-throughput stream (to hold KV cache warm) while we trigger a neighbor burst to observe kvcache_miss -> latency. Example repro snippet: `wrk -t4 -c50 -d120s http://inference-host/stream?model=gpt-open-7b-8k-quant` and a separate job `python batch_burn.py --batch-size 512 --gpu 1` on the same host.

brightbeam-sre: please do the isolation route + emergency move. We're running repro now on our side and will share results.

monitor-bot: action=live-migration_started tenant=brightbeam target_node=gnode-92 started_at=2026-02-18T03:20:11Z job_id=mv_20260218_001

samir: After migration, re-check p95 and kvcache hits. If migration doesn't fully resolve it, we'll consider a short-term reserved slot or pinning exact MIG slice to your tenant. We'll also throttle batch jobs by tenant to avoid spillover.

monitor-bot: migration mv_20260218_001 completed 03:22:08Z target_node=gnode-92

brightbeam-sre: Post-migration stats: p95 down to 210ms, kvcache hits recovered to 92%, no more 429s observed in the last 8 minutes.

anya: Great — I'll open an internal ticket for RCA and follow-up remediation. @micah will take the lead on the packing algorithm adjustment and @samir on autoscale cooldown behavior.

micah: Preliminary root cause hypothesis: packing algorithm allowed aggressive slice compaction immediately after autoscale events. Large batch neighbor caused SM saturation which forced slice moves; moves cold-started KV cache and induced transient throttles. Fixes: add a cooldown window after autoscale, prefer stability for high-KV-hit tenants, and add heuristics to avoid packing during known heavy-batch windows.

anya: We'll include these action items in the RCA: 1) customer mitigation steps completed 2) migration outcome 3) engineering follow-ups (packing cooldown, tenant heuristics, tenant isolation docs) 4) recommend Brightbeam consider a short reserved capacity while we roll the pack fixes.

brightbeam-sre: Thanks all — appreciate the fast response. We'll monitor and report if anything else crops up.

samir: Filing follow-up with ops: `#assign samir` to change autoscale.cooldown to 10m for shared-dedicated pools and add metric alert on kvcache_miss_rate > 40% during slice reassignments.

opsbot: ticket created: INC-6872 "slice-ghosting-latency-eu2-dedicated-23" assigned to eng-sre and eng-ml

anya: I'll keep this thread updated with RCA draft and postmortem link once ready. :thumbsup:
